0.original: Koana is nervously awaiting the call from Thancred.

51.original: I had but to invoke his name. Thancred followed the Hoobigo's boat to its destination, and confirmed that they are indeed holding my sister captive.

52.original: “They,” of course, being Bakool Ja Ja and his minions. I swear, I will make them regret this.

53.original: Lamaty'i is in Richleaf tunnels. The moment the harness is repaired, we strap in the punutiy and make our way back down Ihuykatumu!

54.original: I am glad to see you unharmed, Lamaty'i.

55.original: Thanks again for coming to my rescue, Koana.

57.original: Bakool Ja Ja must be desperate indeed to resort to such aggressive tactics.

58.original: I shouldn't have been so careless. I underestimated him, and it cost me a keystone!

59.original: Fonjeantaine upended his life so that I could accomplish the Moblin's feat. He believed in me─believed in my cause─and I've let him down!

62.original: So we take back what was stolen!

63.original: We won't let Bakool Ja Ja get away with this.

64.original: You're right. It's not over till it's over!

67.original: The next time I meet that brute, I'll knock him straight on his scaly behind and take back my keystone!

68.original: Speaking of vengeance, didn't Bakool Ja Ja curse some “useless Boonewa sycophant” when he caught sight of us?

69.original: A reference to Sareel Ja, I would assume. He is devoted to our brother, and is the only Boonewa I know of participating in the rite of succession.

70.original: If Zoraal Ja was somehow involved in this...

71.original: I will never forgive him for putting our sister in danger! He will have forfeited his right to be called brother!

72.original: Ahem... Bakool Ja Ja should face punishment, of course, but so must the bandits who had the temerity to abduct Lamaty'i.

73.original: I shall request that Father send a contingent of Landsguard to enforce the law in this region.

74.original: I agree that measures need be taken to keep travelers safe.

75.original: But I wonder what pushed these people towards a life of banditry in the first place? If we dig deeper, we might find a way to improve things for everyone.

76.original: ...'Tis something to think about. For now, however, the rite continues. I thank you all for your help.

77.original: We should be moving on, as well. Are you feeling fit to travel, Wuk Lamat?

78.original: You bet I am! Zoraal Ja's gained a good head start, and it's time we clawed back some lost ground!

79.original: Koana is the picture of composure and rationality...except when it comes to matters concerning Wuk Lamat's safety. Far be it from me to fault a brother for being protective, but still.

80.original: The Wuk Lamat I once knew would have been inconsolable at the loss of a keystone.

81.original: This journey─and your companionship─is doing her a world of good.

82.original: We'll need to take that keystone back from Bakool Ja Ja before we arrive at the city of gold. He will not relinquish it without a fight, though...

83.original: Though they share a single body, it's obvious Bakool Ja Ja has two minds when you see one head calming the other head down.

84.original: His personalities are as distinct as two individuals could be.

85.original: I really am sorry this happened. From now on, I won't let my guard down around suspicious strangers.

86.original: And again, I do appreciate you all coming to save me!
